Reviews requested from you, your PRs with failed CI and the reason why, merge conflicts, and PRs ready to merge.
What's on fire
CI red on main, force pushes and direct pushes to protected branches, unreviewed merges, hotfixes to production.
Who's on what
Each person's branches, open PRs, tickets and what they shipped, plus the most active repos and people.
For team leads and CTOs

Made for the Mac

Private
Whoships reads your organization straight from GitHub. Your sign-in stays in your keychain and your GitHub data stays on your Mac.

widgets.title: GitHub Widgets for Mac: PRs, CI and Reviews | Whoships
widgets.description: Put your GitHub organization's pull requests, reviews and CI on your Mac desktop with Whoships widgets in every size. Try it free with sample data.
widgets.h1: GitHub widgets for your Mac desktop
widgets.answer: GitHub has no Mac widgets of its own. Whoships adds them: desktop and Notification Center widgets in small, medium, large and extra large that show your GitHub organization's pull requests, reviews, CI and alerts, and update while Whoships runs.
widgets.imageAlt: Whoships widgets on the Mac desktop: Needs me, Attention, Flow health, Security and CI health
sections: What can a GitHub widget show?

Each widget shows one watcher: Needs me, I'm waiting on, Attention, Who's on what, Active repos, Active people, Flow health, Delivery (DORA), Security or CI health. Or choose Most urgent, which follows whichever watcher has the most severe item. The extra large widget shows two watchers side by side.
How do I add a GitHub widget to my Mac?

1. Download Whoships, open it and sign in with GitHub, or choose Try with sample data.
  2. Control-click the desktop and choose Edit Widgets.
  3. Search for Whoships and drag a widget onto the desktop.
  4. To fix a widget to one watcher, Control-click it and choose Edit “Whoships”.
Do the widgets update on their own?

Yes, whenever Whoships refreshes: your own pull requests every 3 minutes, organization activity every 15 minutes, and delivery, security and CI health every hour. Keep Whoships running with Settings › General › Open at login.
Can I act on a row from the widget?
Click a row to open the pull request, run or alert on GitHub. The round button at the top right switches the widget to the next watcher, and the bell snoozes an item for a day.
faq: Yes. Rows open on GitHub, the switch button changes the watcher, and the bell snoozes an item for a day, all without opening the app.
macOS dims desktop widgets while another app is in front. You can change this in System Settings › Desktop & Dock › Dim widgets on desktop.
Do the widgets work in Notification Center?
Yes. Add them from Edit Widgets in Notification Center as well as on the desktop.

menubar.title: GitHub Menu Bar App for Mac: PRs and Reviews | Whoships
menubar.description: Whoships puts a count of the GitHub pull requests and reviews that need you in your Mac menu bar, one click from the full list. Try it free.
menubar.h1: A GitHub menu bar app for your whole organization
menubar.answer: Whoships puts the number of things that need you in your Mac's menu bar: review requests, your pull requests with failed CI or conflicts, and PRs ready to merge. Click it to see Needs me, I'm waiting on and Attention for your GitHub organization, without opening a browser.
menubar.imageAlt: Whoships cards for Needs me, I'm waiting on and Attention, as shown in the menu bar popover and on the dashboard
sections: What does the menu bar show?

The icon shows the count of items in Needs me. Its popover lists Needs me, I'm waiting on and Attention, the three watchers you check most during the day. Each row opens the pull request or run on GitHub.
How is it different from GitHub notifications?

GitHub notifications are a feed of everything that happened. Whoships shows the current state instead: what is still waiting for you right now, across one organization, with the reason a check failed. Items leave the list when they are done.
Will it notify me?

If you allow notifications, Whoships sends one for new items at warning level and above, or the level you choose. The first refresh after launch only records what is there, so old alerts are not replayed.
How do I set it up?

1. Download Whoships and open it.
  2. Sign in with GitHub and choose your organization.
  3. The Whoships icon appears in the menu bar. Turn on Settings › General › Open at login to keep it there.
faq: Does Whoships stay in the Dock?

Only while one of its windows is open, and only if Settings › General › Show in Dock is on. With its windows closed, Whoships keeps running from the menu bar, and the widgets and dashboard keep updating.
Whoships watches one organization. Personal repositories outside an organization aren't included.
How much GitHub API budget does it use?
About 400 points an hour for a typical organization, well within GitHub's 5,000 an hour. Heavier refreshes pause if the remaining budget runs low.

dashboard.title: GitHub Org Dashboard on Your Mac Desktop | Whoships
dashboard.description: Whoships turns your Mac desktop into a live GitHub organization dashboard: PRs, CI, security and DORA cards on your wallpaper, behind your windows.
dashboard.h1: A GitHub organization dashboard on your desktop
dashboard.answer: Whoships can fill your Mac's desktop with a live dashboard of your GitHub organization. Cards for what needs you, attention, flow health, delivery, security and CI health sit on your wallpaper behind your windows, most urgent first, so a glance at the desktop tells you how the organization is doing.
dashboard.imageAlt: The Whoships desktop dashboard: cards for Needs me, Attention, Security, CI health, Flow health and Delivery on the wallpaper
sections: How does the desktop dashboard work?

Whoships places a borderless window on each display at desktop level, like a live wallpaper. Cards fill the screen in columns, sorted by urgency or in the order you choose. Your windows stay on top of it.
Can I click the cards?
Choose whether the dashboard sits above your desktop icons, where its rows are clickable and open on GitHub, or under them, view only. Open any card's full list to filter it or snooze items.
Which cards can it show?
Any of the ten watchers: Needs me, I'm waiting on, Attention, Who's on what, Active repos, Active people, Flow health, Delivery (DORA), Security and CI health. Hide the ones you don't need.
How do I turn it on?

1. Download Whoships and sign in, or try it with sample data.
  2. Click the Whoships icon in the menu bar.
  3. Switch on Desktop dashboard.
faq: Does it work with several displays?
Yes. The dashboard appears on each display, behind your windows.
Does it slow down my Mac?
No. The dashboard only redraws when Whoships refreshes. Fetching data happens in the background on a schedule.
Is this a replacement for a team TV dashboard?
It's a personal view on your own Mac. For a shared screen, run Whoships on the Mac that drives the screen and turn on the desktop dashboard.

support.title: Whoships Support: Setup, Sign-in and Widgets
support.description: Help with Whoships: signing in to GitHub, organization approval, tokens, widgets, refresh times, the free trial, license keys and removing the app.
support.intro: Questions, problems or ideas: write to macapps.support@icloud.com. Mention your macOS version and what you see.
sections: Getting started

1. Open Whoships. In the Welcome window, click Sign in with GitHub, copy the code, paste it on the GitHub page that opens and click Authorize. Or try everything first with Try with sample data.
  2. Choose the organization to watch.
  3. Add widgets: Control-click the desktop, choose Edit Widgets, search for Whoships and drag a widget onto the desktop.
  4. For the full-desktop dashboard, click the Whoships icon in the menu bar and switch on Desktop dashboard.
“Waiting for your organization to approve Whoships”

Many organizations only let approved apps read their private data. Whoships then shows nothing rather than wrong, empty results. On the waiting screen, click Open Whoships on GitHub to request access, and send an organization owner the ready-made message from Copy message for an owner. Owners approve it under Organization settings › Third-party access › OAuth app policy. Whoships checks every two minutes and starts on its own. A personal access token isn't affected by this approval, if you prefer that.
Signing in with a personal access token

In the Welcome window, choose Use a token. Create a classic token with the repo, read:org and read:user scopes. If your organization uses single sign-on, click Configure SSO next to the token on GitHub and authorize the organization.
Widgets

• Each widget card has a round switch button at the top right that shows the next list. To fix a widget to one list, Control-click it and choose Edit “Whoships”.
  • Widgets update when Whoships refreshes, so keep it running: Settings › General › Open at login.
  • macOS dims desktop widgets while another app is in front; System Settings › Desktop & Dock › Dim widgets on desktop controls this.
How often it refreshes
Your own PRs every 3 minutes, org activity every 15 minutes, and delivery, security and CI health every hour, well within GitHub's hourly API limit. Click the refresh button to update now.
Some cards say “needs org admin access”

Self-hosted runners and outside collaborators need organization admin access, billing needs owner or billing manager access, and security alerts need the features enabled and access to them. Whoships shows everything else and notes what it couldn't read.
Free trial and purchase

Sample data is always free: choose Try with sample data for a made-up organization, no GitHub account needed. With your own organization, Whoships offers a free 14-day trial right after you choose it. After the trial, the one-time purchase Whoships Lifetime keeps it going, with no subscription. Until then, the menu bar and widgets ask you to buy and nothing is read from GitHub. See Pricing.
License keys (bought on whoships.app)

• Unlocking: open Whoships, click Unlock, paste the license key from your purchase email and click Activate.
  • Another Mac: enter the same key on every Mac you personally use.
  • Lost your key? Email us from the address you bought with and we'll send it again.
  • Refunds within 14 days: see the Refund Policy.
App Store purchases

Bought on the Mac App Store? On another Mac, or after reinstalling, open Settings › Account and click Restore Purchases. The trial and Whoships Lifetime belong to your Apple Account, so the trial can be taken once. For refunds, use reportaproblem.apple.com, since Apple handles App Store payments.
Signing out
Settings › Account › Sign out deletes your sign-in and all fetched data from your Mac. To revoke Whoships's access on GitHub too, open GitHub › Settings › Applications.
Removing Whoships
Sign out first if you want to delete its data, then quit Whoships and move it to the Trash. Nothing on GitHub is affected: Whoships only reads.

faq.title: Whoships FAQ: GitHub Dashboard and Widgets for Mac
faq.description: Answers about Whoships, the Mac app for your GitHub organization: what it reads, privacy, organization approval, pricing, refresh times and requirements.
items: What is Whoships?

Whoships is a Mac app that shows one GitHub organization's pull requests, reviews, CI, security alerts and DORA metrics in desktop widgets, the menu bar and a dashboard that fills your desktop. It answers what needs you, what you're waiting on, who is working on what and what's on fire.
Who is Whoships for?

Staff engineers, team leads, engineering managers and CTOs who want to know what matters in their organization without opening twenty browser tabs. Individual developers use Needs me and I'm waiting on to keep their own pull requests moving.
Is my code or data sent to your servers?

No. Only the app talks to GitHub. Your sign-in stays in your Mac's keychain, and what Whoships reads stays on your Mac. The App Store version sends nothing to us. The version from whoships.app sends anonymous usage statistics, without any GitHub data, which you can turn off in Settings › General.
Does Whoships change anything on GitHub?
No. Whoships only reads. It never comments, approves, merges, re-runs or changes settings.
Do I need my organization's approval?

If your organization restricts OAuth apps, an owner approves Whoships once. Whoships helps you request it and copies a ready-made message for an owner. A personal access token works without that approval.
Can I try it without signing in?
Yes. Try with sample data fills every watcher, widget and the dashboard with a made-up organization, with no GitHub account. Sample data is always free.
How much does Whoships cost?
Watching your own organization is free for 14 days. Then Whoships Lifetime is a one-time purchase of €19.99 / US$19.99, with updates to Whoships 1 included. There is no subscription.
How often does it refresh?

Your own pull requests every 3 minutes, organization activity every 15 minutes, and delivery, security and CI health every hour. A typical organization uses about 400 of GitHub's 5,000 API points an hour.
Does it measure DORA metrics?
Yes. The Delivery watcher measures deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore from GitHub Deployments, releases or merges to production branches.
Can I watch more than one organization?
Whoships watches one organization at a time. You can switch organizations in Settings.
Does it work with GitHub Enterprise?
Whoships works with organizations on github.com, including those on GitHub Enterprise Cloud. GitHub Enterprise Server isn't supported yet.
Does it work on iPhone, Windows or Linux?
No. Whoships is a Mac app and needs macOS 26 or later.
Is Whoships made by GitHub?
No. Whoships is made by an independent developer and is not affiliated with GitHub, Inc. It uses GitHub's public API with your own account.
